#001

Heading hierarchy may be inconsistent

heading-order  •  UF-00001
Medium Custom + axe Headings WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships Level A High - detected by both engines
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Unexpected heading-level jumps can make the relationship between sections harder to understand.

Location

DOM selector: #research-section > .row > .font-weight-600.font-28.line-bottom | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<h4 class="text-uppercase font-weight-600 mt-0 font-28 line-bottom" style="padding-left: 15px; margin-bottom: 25px; "><ion-icon name="library-outline"></ion-icon> RESEARCH ACTIVITIES<span class="view-all"><a href="all-research">view all research →</a></span></h4>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Heading order invalid

Custom scanner evidence

Heading level jumps from H2 to H4.

axe description

Ensure the order of headings is semantically correct

Recommended change

Review the document outline and use heading levels according to the logical content hierarchy.

Manual review

Required: Yes

A heading-level jump is not automatically a WCAG failure. The full document hierarchy must be reviewed.

#005

Link does not have a discernible accessible name

link-name  •  UF-00005
High Custom + axe Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A High - detected by both engines
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Screen-reader users may encounter a link without being told what it does or where it goes.

Location

DOM selector: .xs-pull-right | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a class="menuzord-brand pull-right flip xs-pull-right mb-15" href="javascript:void(0)">
                  <!--<img src="https://ku.ac.bd/uploads/student-feedback-form.png" alt="Not Found" title="Student Handbook" />-->
                </a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

Custom scanner evidence

Link has no accessible name. Add meaningful link text, aria-label, or image alt text.

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Suggested code pattern 

<a aria-label="Describe link destination" class="menuzord-brand pull-right flip xs-pull-right mb-15" href="javascript:void(0)">
<!--<img src="https://ku.ac.bd/uploads/student-feedback-form.png" alt="Not Found" title="Student Handbook" />-->
</a>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

#020

Image has an empty alternative

empty_alt  •  UF-00020
Medium Custom Images WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content Level A Contextual/manual review Context-aware recommendation
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Empty alt text is appropriate for decorative images but may hide meaningful content when used on informative images.

Location

DOM selector: section#home > div.container-fluid.p-0 > div.rev_slider_wrapper > div.rev_slider > ul > li:nth-of-type(1) > img.rev-slidebg | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<img alt="" class="rev-slidebg" data-bgfit="cover" data-bgparallax="10" data-bgposition="center 40%" data-bgrepeat="no-repeat" data-no-retina="" src="uploads/sliders/1753781253rsz_rsz_dsc_1215_copy.jpg"/>

Custom scanner evidence

Image has an empty alt attribute.

Recommended change

Keep alt="" if the image is decorative. If the image communicates information or performs a function, replace the empty value with meaningful alternative text.

Context-Aware Recommendation

Visually inspect the image. If it communicates information related to “Khulna University”, replace alt="" with a concise description of what the image actually communicates. If it is purely decorative, keep alt="".

Why this suggestion was made: The surrounding nearby heading identifies the content context, but textual context alone cannot determine what the image visually contains.

Evidence: nearby heading Context confidence: medium Language: en Decision: EMPTY_ALT_CONTEXT_AVAILABLE

Recommended action: verify decorative or informative

Visual review required

The surrounding text provides contextual evidence, but the image itself must be inspected before final alternative text is written.

Human verification: Required before implementation.

This recommendation was generated by the proposed deterministic contextual decision engine. Context confidence describes the strength of the extracted contextual evidence, not WCAG conformance certainty.

Suggested code pattern 

<img alt="[Describe image if informative]" class="rev-slidebg" data-bgfit="cover" data-bgparallax="10" data-bgposition="center 40%" data-bgrepeat="no-repeat" data-no-retina="" src="uploads/sliders/1753781253rsz_rsz_dsc_1215_copy.jpg"/>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Automation cannot reliably determine whether the image is decorative or informative.

#042

Image alternative text may not be descriptive

non_descriptive_alt  •  UF-00042
Medium Custom Images WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content Level A Custom automated finding Context-aware recommendation
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Although the image has an alt attribute, generic text such as 'image', 'thumbnail', 'news image', 'event image', or a filename may not communicate the image's actual content or purpose.

Location

DOM selector: div#child-1 > li.list-group-item > div.panel > img.panel-img-top | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<img alt="No image" class="panel-img-top" height="225" src="uploads/research-publication/Capture070620221137.JPG" width="330"/>

Custom scanner evidence

Alt text is generic and does not describe the image's content or purpose.

Recommended change

Review the purpose of the image and replace generic or filename-like alternative text with a concise description that communicates the same relevant information or function. If the image is purely decorative, use alt="" instead.

Context-Aware Recommendation

Replace the generic alt text “No image” after visually inspecting the image. The surrounding context “RESEARCH ACTIVITIES view all research →” can guide the description, but should not be copied as alt text unless it accurately represents the image.

Why this suggestion was made: The current alt attribute exists but appears non-descriptive. Context provides evidence about the related content, not proof of the image's visual content.

Evidence: nearby heading Context confidence: medium Language: en Decision: GENERIC_ALT_CONTEXT_AVAILABLE

Recommended action: replace generic alt after visual review

Visual review required

The surrounding text provides contextual evidence, but the image itself must be inspected before final alternative text is written.

Human verification: Required before implementation.

This recommendation was generated by the proposed deterministic contextual decision engine. Context confidence describes the strength of the extracted contextual evidence, not WCAG conformance certainty.

Suggested code pattern 

<img alt="[Replace with a meaningful context-specific description]" class="panel-img-top" height="225" src="uploads/research-publication/Capture070620221137.JPG" width="330"/>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Alternative-text quality depends on the image's purpose and surrounding context. The automated rule identifies likely non-descriptive text but does not by itself establish a WCAG failure.

DOM selector: body | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Manual review

Required: Yes

color-contrast  •  UF-00183
Review axe — manual review Color contrast WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Level AA Manual review required
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Location

DOM selector: h6 > a[href="/event-details/1846"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a href="/event-details/1846">খুবিতে ‘লেট’স কোড ইউর ক্যারিয়ার থ্রু প্রোগ্রামিং’ শীর্ষক কর্মশালা অনুষ্ঠিত</a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element's background color could not be determined due to a background gradient

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

Why this matters

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Methodology note: Automated accessibility testing can identify many important problems, but it cannot establish complete WCAG conformance. Context-dependent and incomplete findings require human review. Context-aware recommendations are produced by deterministic rules using extracted local page context and should be verified before implementation.
